universal_observations.name: Nominal capability versus effective usable capacity
universal_observations.definition: A rated, allocated, predicted, or demonstrated capability becomes economically usable only after workload fit, availability, yield, topology, contention, process control, qualification, and decision rules are applied.
universal_observations.canonical_logic: nominal capability -> constraint- and regime-conditioned availability -> effective usable capacity -> good output or service
diagnostic_questions: Is the measure local or system-wide?
Is the output good, released, and deliverable?
Which workload and operating regime apply?

universal_observations.name: Constraint migration under scaling
universal_observations.definition: Relieving or scaling one constraint changes the system state and often moves the binding limit to communication, memory, thermal management, packaging, scheduling, qualification, power, supply, or organizational coordination.
universal_observations.canonical_logic: local relief or scale-up -> changed flows and coupling -> new binding constraint -> revised effective output
diagnostic_questions: What was binding before the intervention?
Which downstream resource absorbs the added flow?
Does the effect persist at higher load or complexity?
Did robustness or coordination cost change?
common_failures: Projecting benchmark gains into industrial complexity.
Assuming packaging or interconnect is passive.
Assuming more starts always increase good output.
Treating policy at one layer as chain-wide resilience.

universal_observations.name: Unit efficiency versus aggregate scale demand
universal_observations.definition: Lower resource use per unit of work does not determine aggregate resource demand when workload volume, model size, test-time compute, service quality, utilization, or adoption changes.
universal_observations.canonical_logic: unit resource intensity x workload volume x quality/scale factor x facility overhead = aggregate resource demand
diagnostic_questions: Is energy measured at device, node, cluster, or facility?
Are idle and cooling loads included?
common_failures: Inferring lower total electricity from lower joules per token.
Using latency as an energy proxy.
Extending a server configuration to the fleet.

universal_observations.name: Technical feasibility versus commercial realization
universal_observations.definition: A technically feasible device, process, architecture, pilot, award, or announced investment becomes commercial output only through integration, manufacturability, qualification, construction, ramp, customer adoption, and stable volume.
universal_observations.canonical_logic: concept or award -> engineering demonstration -> integrated system -> qualified process/product -> released capacity -> stable commercial output
diagnostic_questions: Which realization stage is directly observed?
Has the integrated product been qualified?
Is output repeatable at relevant volume and yield?
Is demand articulated into an adopted commercial product?
